subject: Civil Engineering
title: Types of Spillways
description: A 60-second lesson on Types of Spillways.

hook.text: Not all spillways pour over the dam crest — some use tunnels, shafts, or side channels.

buildup.text: Chute spillways send water down a steep concrete channel on the dam's side — fast and controlled.

discovery.text: Shaft (glory hole) spillways drain through a vertical hole — water spirals down like a bathtub drain.

twist.text: Side channel spillways run parallel to the dam — the water turns 90 degrees before descending.

climax.text: Labyrinth spillways use zigzag crests — fitting more overflow length in less width.

punchline.text: Every dam needs an exit for floods. The spillway type depends on the site and the flood.

quiz.question: How does a labyrinth spillway handle more water than a straight-crested spillway?
options: It uses pumps to accelerate water flow over the crest
Its zigzag crest provides more overflow length in the same width
It diverts water underground through multiple tunnels

details.summary: Spillway types include overflow or ogee spillways that water flows over like a waterfall, side channel spillways that run along the dam's side, shaft or morning glory spillways that drain through a vertical funnel.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing the right spillway type determines whether a dam can safely pass extreme floods. Each type suits specific site conditions, dam types, and discharge requirements.
takeaways: Ogee spillways create an efficient overflow profile matched to water trajectory
Morning glory spillways are vertical funnels suited to narrow canyon sites
Labyrinth spillways multiply effective crest length for higher capacity

faq.question: How does a labyrinth spillway increase discharge capacity?
faq.answer: A labyrinth spillway folds the crest into a zigzag or trapezoidal plan shape, increasing the total crest length within the same overall width. Since spillway discharge is proportional to crest length.

faq.question: What is a morning glory or shaft spillway?
faq.answer: A morning glory spillway is a circular funnel-shaped intake that water spirals into and drains through a vertical shaft connected to a tunnel passing under or around the dam.
